text_post: Quaker State full synthetic now, Castrol GTX in the past. I know that some people had bad experiences with waxy deposits from running QS (conventional) decades ago but according to the experts, the full synthetic product is a very good oil. Change it every 6,000 to 7,000 miles in my daily driver and twice per year in the weekend car. Filters are either OEM, or Mobil 1. According to the oil experts, it really doesn’t matter that much what brand you use. Changing it at appropriate intervals and running the correct viscosity is much more critical. The daily-driver (Ford truck) has accumulated nearly a quarter-million miles. Had over a quarter-million on a (retired and gone) Honda. Had 198,000 miles on a Nissan, when a deer retired it for me. Not a single oil-related problem, ever.

I used to get mostly Penzoil or Shell. However, been getting Motorcraft latley, I find it just as affordably priced at the local auto stores as the store brand dino-juice plus its made specific for Ford engines. I have a early 2000’s Mazda that has a Ford engine. In my Mazda I use the factory recommended weight non-senthetic. Back when I had my GMC G20, Chevy C1500, BMW735I, Ford Festiva and Ford Diesel trucks (6.9, and 7.3 Powerstroke), they all lived in Shell RotellaT 15W40 Diesel oil. I had those over a span of time not all at once. Never ever had an issue in any of these vehicles with the oil. It seemed to work just as good and I remember having better results. These were all older higher mileage vehicles and I could get away with heavier oil. I am not recommending you go out and dump RotellaT 15W40 in your vehicle, it just worked very well for me in a wide span of vehicles and I had good results. The Diesel oil did excellent in the gassers, stronger levels of deturgent I believe. Now in newer vehicles I wouldnt use but the recommended weight, the tolerances are much tighter on new machines. I also do not use synthetic oil unless the engine is designed for it. Other wise I believe synthetic is a waste of money.
